tasks.title: Task 8
tasks.statement: Using the starchart (Fig.1) answer the following questions:

parts.question: What is the ecliptic latitude of the galactic center? Answer: β = _________ deg
The positions of four objects from the Messier catalog are indicated using Latin letters. Which are these objects? A: M______ B: M_______ C: M________ D: M________
parts.reference:
A: M7
B: M6
C: M4
D: M80

tasks.title: Task 9
tasks.statement: All eight stars brighter than 2 mag have been erased from the map (Fig.2).

parts.question: Fill in their positions and names (e.g. Deneb or α Cyg) back on the map.
parts.reference: Fill in the positions and names back on the map. (0.25 pts for position, 0.25 pts for name, a total of 4 pts for 8 stars)

parts.question: Which constellation is exactly in the southwestern (SW) corner of the map? Write its standard three-letter Latin designation. Answer: ___________

tasks.title: Task 10
tasks.statement: The diagram (Fig.3) shows how the altitude of three stars above the horizon changes during a night near the winter solstice as observed from the Rozhen observatory (41°41′N, 24°44′E). The one-digit numbers on the chart are the numbers of the stars, while the two-digit numbers are angular distances from the moon in degrees.

parts.question:
What are the equatorial coordinates of the three stars?
Star 1: α = _________ h δ = ________ deg
Star 2: α = _________ h δ = ________ deg
Star 3: α = _________ h δ = ________ deg
parts.reference:
Star 1: α = 9h δ = +79 deg
Star 2: α = 5h δ = -13 deg
Star 3: α = 10h δ = +22 deg

parts.question:
How many days after the preceding new moon is this night?
Answer: t = ________ d

tasks.title: Task 11
tasks.statement: This image of a field around a quasar is obtained with a 35-cm telescope. It is one of the following four quasars (on the finder charts on Fig. 5):

parts.question:
Which quasar is on the image? Identify the field and circle the correct answer.
Answer: 3C 66A / OJ 287 / 3C 454.3 / PKS 1510-08

What changes have to be made in the equatorial coordinates of the telescope in order to put the quasar in the center of the field?
Answer: Δα = _________ ′′ Δδ = _________ ′′

Approximate distances to some field stars are indicated on the charts in parsecs. Estimate roughly the distance to the quasar:
Answer: d = _________ pc
parts.reference:
0 pts: d < 1 Mpc or d > 15 Gpc
0.5 pts: d = 1 – 99 Mpc
1 pt: d = 100 Mpc – 15 Gpc
A trick question. The actual quasar is at z=0.306, corresponding to a distance of ~1 Gpc, which cannot be derived from the charts. The nearest active quasar known is at a distance of ~180 Mpc.

What is the geographical latitude of the location of the observation that the software is simulating? North or south of the equator (underline the correct option)?
